title: Sprite Work Continues for Latest Project (TBA June 30)
author: Fun_Worry_3079
selftext: Sprite work has continued on my latest project. So far, I've created over 100 unique sprites for this game (though, I must admit, not all of them will appear in the final project). It's going to be a tough job, animating them all in PixelLab, but I look forward to the process!

comments.author: Donjuante
comments.body:
Why do the ones at the top have such big heads? Especially the last two, the guy with the clock on his armor and the mage. They're humans, so it doesn't make sense for them to have such large heads.

https://preview.redd.it/mn0g2a6odx9h1.png?width=245&format=png&auto=webp&s=4e68538e3e0bc6ba8adbf7130cb451b2d24b6642

replies.author: Fun_Worry_3079
replies.body:
These sprites were generated in separate sessions, so some variance among them is inevitable. I had made a conscious choice, however, to keep these characters in their current iteration because I wanted them to be the "recognizables;" characters with which players connect. The other humans, such as the shopkeepers and villagers, don't really add much to the story (if at all), so they could be rather generic-looking humans. The main four characters (as well as the villain, the blue snake in robes) to be the emphasis of the game, so natually I chose their larger proportions to give them more character and expression (to be added later).

Sorry if this answer is a bit long, but I just felt that giving "design context" was important.

comments.author: Longjumping_Bit_1546
comments.body: The individual designs are great, but what really stands out is how cohesive the whole set feels. You can tell a lot of thought and care went into these — seriously impressive work!

comments.author: SleazyF
comments.body: What did you use to generate these? Looks great!

replies.author: Fun_Worry_3079
replies.body: These were generated using the PixelLab extension in Aseprite. Thank you for enjoying them!
